findings.issue: Ignoring EPERM is correct: the helper no longer crashes, and the round-1 NIT killgroup-eperm-uncaught is resolved. One gap remains. If both the timeout SIGTERM and the SIGKILL fail with EPERM (for example, only a root-owned sudo is left in the helper's group), the child never exits. runAttempt resolves only on 'exit' or 'error', so the attempt never settles. There is no retry and no ::error:: line. The helper just waits until the step's timeout-minutes: 13 cancels it. This is not a hidden failure: the step still fails, and the job timeout (20 min) also bounds it. So the change fails closed, but slowly and with an unclear message.
findings.evidence: sudo (euid root) is left alone in the helper-created pgid -> timeout -> killGroup(-pid, SIGTERM) gets EPERM and logs it -> killGroup(-pid, SIGKILL) gets EPERM and logs it -> no 'exit' event -> the promise stays pending -> the step-level timeout-minutes kills the step and it fails. No untrusted input is involved.
findings.fix: Optional: if the SIGKILL from the kill timer also gets EPERM, resolve the attempt as 'could not be killed (EPERM)' and fail the helper fast with a clear ::error::, instead of waiting for the step timeout. Keep timeout-minutes on both steps either way. The Linux-CI sudo test, with its 30 s Vitest timeout, will show whether this happens on ubuntu-24.04.

findings.issue: Carried over from round 1 and unchanged by this commit. finish() sends SIGKILL to -child.pid after the child has been reaped. In theory that PGID could have been reused in the meantime. There is no realistic path to this.
findings.evidence: child 'exit' -> finish() -> killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL'). No untrusted input controls the PID or the timing.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. (1) Shell injection: the sudo test passes argv as an array to spawn and then to the helper, which also spawns with no shell. The only shell is sh -c 'exec sleep "$1"'. Its script is a constant, and the marker is a quoted positional parameter built from crypto.randomInt digits ("1000.<9 digits>"). Nothing untrusted reaches it, so there is no injection. (2) Running sudo in tests: the real-sudo test runs under describe.skipIf(!(process.platform === 'linux' && process.env.CI === 'true')). On macOS or any local run it is skipped; I confirmed this locally (3 passed, 1 skipped). sudo -n never prompts. Without passwordless sudo it fails at once and the test fails, which is harmless. With passwordless sudo it only runs sleep as root for about 2 s per attempt. Worst case, if killing fails, a root sleep lasting about 1000 s is left on a single-use runner. A Linux developer who exports CI=true and has passwordless sudo would also run it; the effect is the same and benign. The killGroup unit tests replace process.kill with a mock (restored in afterEach), so no real signal is ever sent locally. (3) Ignoring EPERM: only EPERM and ESRCH are ignored. Every other errno is still rethrown, and a test covers that (EINVAL). EPERM is logged with a 'retry:' line, so it is visible. Ignoring it cannot turn a failed install into a success. The helper exits 0 only when the child exits with code 0, and timedOut forces a failure reason. The worst case is the slow-fail hang described in the MINOR above, which the step's timeout-minutes bounds. No new dependencies; node:crypto randomInt is built in. Round-1 NIT killgroup-eperm-uncaught: fixed.
